question.problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the finite region bounded between the circles ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=2$ and ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1?$

I. It is a type I region

II. It is a type II region

III. It's neither a type I nor a type II region
question.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14131515/assets/28290c5530efd27a979f4284481ca7e0384342d7d426dde0ab36894a0d77a166.png)

We have the following:

- The vertical line $x=0.5$ intersects the region in two separate intervals, as shown below. So, this can't be a type I region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14131515/assets/3007cffb725faee44d2a06ad077eec630791b1a94c373a323f62d0d721c87207.png)

- The horizontal line $y=0.5$ intersects the region in two separate intervals, as shown below. So, this can't be a type II region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14131515/assets/383f88668435556d3a856cf852caf548b1f1bf3a90d50f9d85d7968188984804.png)

Therefore, only statement III is true.
